## Rates for the 2025-26 income year

For the 2025-26 income year, a resident individual pays no tax on the first
$18,200 of taxable income. Income between $18,201 and $45,000 is taxed at 16c
for each $1 over $18,200. From $45,001 to $135,000 the tax is $4,288 plus 30c
for each $1 over $45,000. From $135,001 to $190,000 the tax is $31,288 plus 37c
for each $1 over $135,000. Above $190,000 the tax is $51,638 plus 45c for each
$1 over $190,000. These amounts do not include the Medicare levy of 2%.

## Rates for the 2024-25 income year

The 2024-25 income year uses the same brackets and rates as 2025-26: nil to
$18,200, then 16c in the dollar to $45,000, then $4,288 plus 30c to $135,000,
then $31,288 plus 37c to $190,000, then $51,638 plus 45c above that. The
Medicare levy is not included.

## Rates for the 2023-24 income year

For 2023-24 the first $18,200 was tax free. Income from $18,201 to $45,000 was
taxed at 19c for each $1 over $18,200. From $45,001 to $120,000 the tax was
$5,092 plus 32.5c for each $1 over $45,000. From $120,001 to $180,000 it was
$29,467 plus 37c for each $1 over $120,000, and above $180,000 it was $51,667
plus 45c for each $1 over $180,000.

## Rates for the 2026-27 income year

For the 2026-27 income year the first $18,200 remains tax free. Income from
$18,201 to $45,000 is taxed at 15c for each $1 over $18,200. From $45,001 to
$135,000 the tax is $4,020 plus 30c for each $1 over $45,000. From $135,001 to
$190,000 it is $31,020 plus 37c for each $1 over $135,000, and above $190,000
it is $51,370 plus 45c for each $1 over $190,000.
